beats.label: S1 · Bullock and Hickok arrive
beats.text: Ex-marshal Seth Bullock arrives to open a hardware store; his ally Wild Bill Hickok kills a man tied to the Metz family murder, angering camp boss Al Swearengen.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the three-way axis — Bullock, Hickok, Al — that defines the camp before Hickok is removed from it.

beats.label: S1 · Al kills Garret, Hickok dies
beats.text: Al has newcomer Brom Garret murdered for his gold claim; prospector Ellsworth witnesses it. Widow Alma asks Hickok for help before he is shot dead at the poker table.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Creates the two engines of the rest of the season: the Garret claim as the prize Al wants, and the absence Hickok's death leaves for Bullock to fill.

beats.label: S1 · Sofia saved, Alma takes her in
beats.text: With the Metz killers dead and Sofia no longer a threat to identify them, Al allows her a safe return to Deadwood, where Alma later takes her in.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sofia is the reason Alma stays in camp, which is the reason her claim stays contested — the trigger for every Alma beat that follows.

beats.label: S1 · Bullock becomes Alma's protector
beats.text: Hardened by his hunt for Hickok's killer, Bullock puts himself between Alma and Al's frontmen when they try to buy her now-valuable claim on the cheap.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up both the affair and the political rivalry that everything in season 2 is built on.

beats.label: S1 · Smallpox forces cooperation
beats.text: A smallpox outbreak forces Al to pool money with rival Cy Tolliver and the camp's leaders for vaccine, exposing Deadwood's need for something like a government.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First moment the camp acts collectively; the practice run for the interim government they cobble together next.

beats.label: S1 · Annexation and interim government
beats.text: Word arrives that Deadwood will be annexed by Dakota Territory; Al bribes a magistrate to install an interim government while dodging a murder warrant on himself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Annexation is the pressure that shapes every political move in season 2; the interim government is the frame Bullock will step into.

beats.label: S1 · Bullock takes the badge
beats.text: Al smothers the dying Reverend Smith and has the magistrate killed; Bullock walks into the Gem to declare himself sheriff, splitting the camp's power in two.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The final tableau of the season and the exact starting position of season 2: sheriff vs saloon owner, with a fragile understanding between them.

cliffhanger.text: Bullock has claimed the sheriff's badge and set himself opposite Al Swearengen as Deadwood braces for annexation, its lawless order suddenly having to answer to a lawman.
questions: Can Bullock actually enforce law in a camp Al still effectively runs?
Will Alma's affair with Bullock survive the arrival of formal government — and the wife he has not mentioned?
What does annexation cost the men who built Deadwood outside the law?

characters.name: Seth Bullock
characters.line: Ex-marshal turned hardware store owner; hot-tempered and just made himself sheriff of the camp.

characters.name: Al Swearengen
characters.line: Owner of the Gem saloon and de facto ruler of Deadwood; a ruthless political operator now forced to share power.

characters.name: Alma Garret
characters.line: Widowed heiress to the richest gold claim in camp, recovering laudanum addict, guardian of the orphan Sofia, and in love with Bullock.

characters.name: Cy Tolliver
characters.line: Owner of the rival Bella Union saloon; a smoother, more sadistic version of Al.

characters.name: E.B. Farnum
characters.line: Manager of the Grand Central Hotel, Al's fawning fixer, and the interim mayor.

characters.name: Trixie
characters.line: Al's favored prostitute at the Gem; drawn to Bullock's partner Sol Star.

characters.name: Sol Star
characters.line: Bullock's steady-headed business partner and Trixie's discreet lover.

characters.name: Doc Cochran
characters.line: The camp doctor and its moral conscience; the reason Sofia is still alive.

characters.name: Whitney Ellsworth
characters.line: Grizzled prospector working Alma's claim; the only man who saw Brom Garret murdered and stayed quiet about it.

beats.label: S2 · Martha arrives, affair ends
beats.text: Seven months on, Bullock and Alma's affair continues until his wife Martha and stepson William arrive from Michigan, forcing him to end it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes Bullock from Alma's lover to the man who chose duty, which is the position he defends for the rest of the season.

beats.label: S2 · Bullock and Al ally against annexation
beats.text: Bullock and Al brawl in the street over the camp's future, then forge an uneasy alliance to shape Deadwood's annexation on their own terms.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's political spine: the two enemies become partners of convenience, a pact that has to hold against everything Hearst sends next.

beats.label: S2 · Wolcott arrives buying claims
beats.text: Geologist Francis Wolcott arrives buying claims for the unseen tycoon George Hearst; Cy Tolliver quietly makes himself Hearst's other man in camp.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Hearst as an off-screen force and Tolliver as his willing servant — the outside pressure the Bullock/Al alliance is now defending against.

beats.label: S2 · Alma pregnant, marries Ellsworth
beats.text: Alma learns she is pregnant by Bullock; Trixie pushes the loyal prospector Ellsworth to marry her and give the child a name, and Alma accepts.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks in the household Hearst will later target — Alma, Ellsworth, Sofia, and a coming child — and quietly ends any return to the affair.

beats.label: S2 · Wolcott murders the prostitutes
beats.text: Wolcott murders three prostitutes at Joanie Stubbs's brothel, exposing his sadism and turning Charlie Utter against Tolliver, who covers for him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The scandal that fatally weakens Wolcott and forces Hearst to come to Deadwood in person to clean it up.

beats.label: S2 · William dies, Martha stays
beats.text: William is trampled by a runaway horse and dies; Martha decides to stay in Deadwood as its schoolteacher rather than take her grief home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Anchors Martha into the town and gives the Bullock marriage the shared wound it will operate from afterwards.

beats.label: S2 · Hearst arrives, annexation signed
beats.text: Hearst arrives in person, fires and disowns Wolcott (who hangs himself), and buys the Grand Central as Deadwood is formally annexed at Alma's wedding to Ellsworth.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The exact starting position of season 3: Hearst inside the camp, the pact against him already made, the disgraced Wolcott gone.

cliffhanger.text: Deadwood is officially annexed and George Hearst is now living in it, having bought his way in. Bullock walks out of an empty Gem alone into a town that is no longer his to shape.
questions: What does Hearst intend to do with a claim-hungry town he now largely controls?
Can Bullock and Martha's marriage carry the weight of William's death?
Where does Alma's marriage of convenience to Ellsworth leave her — and the child she is carrying by Bullock?

characters.name: Seth Bullock
characters.line: Sheriff of Deadwood; ended the affair with Alma when his wife arrived, and has just buried his stepson.

characters.name: Al Swearengen
characters.line: Gem owner recovering from kidney stones and a stroke; in uneasy alliance with Bullock against Hearst.

characters.name: Alma Garret
characters.line: Pregnant by Bullock and newly married to Ellsworth for propriety; owns the single richest claim Hearst wants.

characters.name: George Hearst
characters.line: The mining tycoon Wolcott worked for, now living in Deadwood having bought the Grand Central; intends to own every claim in camp.

characters.name: Cy Tolliver
characters.line: Bella Union owner; helped cover up Wolcott's murders, was stabbed by the minister Cramed, and is now leveraged into working for Hearst.

characters.name: Whitney Ellsworth
characters.line: The prospector who works Alma's claim and is now her husband and father to her child in name.

characters.name: Trixie
characters.line: Has left the Gem to keep books for Sol Star; steered Alma into Ellsworth's arms to protect the pregnancy.

characters.name: Martha Bullock
characters.line: Bullock's grieving wife; has chosen to stay in Deadwood as its schoolteacher rather than flee William's death.

characters.name: Doc Cochran
characters.line: The camp doctor; pulled Al through his stroke.

beats.label: S3 · Hearst pushes, old enemies unite
beats.text: Hearst moves to dominate the camp, killing miners who resist him; Bullock and Al set aside their feud to hold a fragile united front against him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames the season as a siege: everything after is a test of whether that alliance can hold under Hearst's escalating pressure.

beats.label: S3 · Alma's pregnancy nearly kills her
beats.text: Alma's difficult pregnancy nearly kills her, requiring surgery she barely survives; Bullock swears to protect her and Sofia if Hearst moves on the claim.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Alma physically at her weakest just as Hearst decides she is the prize, and locks Bullock into her defence.

beats.label: S3 · Hearst cuts off Al's finger
beats.text: When Al refuses to be strong-armed into helping Hearst take Alma's claim, Hearst himself cuts off Al's finger — and Al still refuses.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moment Hearst stops pretending to negotiate; also proves Al will not sell Alma out even under mutilation.

beats.label: S3 · Alma relapses, Ellsworth moves out
beats.text: Alma relapses into laudanum under the strain; Ellsworth moves out of their house, blaming himself for making her miserable.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Isolates both spouses — the exact vulnerability Hearst exploits when he decides Ellsworth is the way to break her.

beats.label: S3 · Ellsworth killed, Trixie shoots Hearst
beats.text: Hearst has Ellsworth murdered to force Alma to sell; Trixie storms the Grand Central and shoots Hearst, only wounding him in the shoulder.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's pivot — the escalation that removes Alma's protector and puts Trixie under a death sentence.

beats.label: S3 · Al kills Jen to save Trixie
beats.text: To spare Trixie, Al kills the prostitute Jen — Trixie's rough lookalike — and delivers her body to Hearst as proof of vengeance.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moral hinge of Al's arc: he pays for the town's defiance with a body of his own choosing, and the camp's power sits with him again in exactly the way he hates.

beats.label: S3 · Hearst wins the election and leaves
beats.text: Broken, Alma sells her claim to Hearst; his imported soldiers rig the election to install his sheriff, and Hearst rides out of Deadwood untouched.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season ends with Hearst winning on every axis he cared about, which is the state of the town everyone is left to live in.

cliffhanger.text: Hearst has left camp with Alma's claim in his pocket and his sheriff in Bullock's old chair, while Al scrubs Jen's blood off the Gem floor and lies to a grieving Johnny that she did not suffer.
questions: Was killing Jen enough to keep Hearst from ever coming back for Trixie?
Can Deadwood be anything other than a Hearst company town from here?
What is left of Alma after losing Ellsworth, her claim, and her independence in the same week?

characters.name: Seth Bullock
characters.line: Sheriff for most of the season; unseated in the rigged election that installed Hearst's man Harry Manning.

characters.name: Al Swearengen
characters.line: Gem owner, missing a finger to Hearst, who murdered the prostitute Jen to pass off as Trixie and end the feud.

characters.name: Alma Ellsworth
characters.line: Widowed a second time and forced to sell her claim to Hearst; still owns the bank and still raising Sofia.

characters.name: George Hearst
characters.line: The mining tycoon who broke Deadwood to his will and left camp with the sheriff's post and Alma's claim in his pocket.

characters.name: Trixie
characters.line: Bookkeeper at Alma's bank; shot Hearst in revenge for Ellsworth and lives only because Al covered for her with Jen's body.

characters.name: Whitney Ellsworth
characters.line: Alma's husband, murdered on Hearst's orders — the death that triggered the season's endgame.

characters.name: Cy Tolliver
characters.line: Bella Union owner reduced to a low-ranking servant of Hearst's operation; took out his humiliation by killing his own man Leon.

characters.name: Sol Star
characters.line: Bullock's partner and Trixie's protector; sheltered her at the Gem after the shooting.

characters.name: Doc Cochran
characters.line: The camp doctor, showing symptoms of tuberculosis and planning to leave town for everyone's safety, though Al demands he stay.
